entries.name: Louvre Museum
entries.era: Medieval fortress; later royal palace; public museum since 1793
entries.geometry: Palace wings and courtyards around the Cour Napoléon; glass pyramid entrance; complex interior galleries
entries.materials: Limestone masonry, stone sculpture, metal-and-glass pyramid
capture: Louvre Palace courtyard elevations and wing-by-wing facades
Pyramid geometry and courtyard ground plan
Gallery circulation, ceiling heights and staircase references
Stone weathering, window modules and night illumination
entries.cautions: Separate medieval, royal-palace and contemporary museum periods; avoid inventing interior floor plans.

entries.name: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History
entries.era: Opened 1910; Smithsonian museum on the National Mall
entries.geometry: Monumental Beaux-Arts building with central rotunda and gallery wings
entries.materials: Stone exterior, masonry, glass exhibition cases and varied interior finishes
capture: Exhibition hall layouts and gallery transitions
Display-case lighting and large exhibit clearances
entries.cautions: Exhibitions change; document the reference year for any reconstructed gallery.

entries.name: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
entries.era: National Mall museum opened 1976; major renovations in the 2020s
entries.geometry: Long museum frontage with large exhibition halls and aerospace display volumes
entries.materials: Stone and glass exterior, metal aerospace artifacts, modern gallery finishes
capture: Exterior facade modules and main entry
entries.cautions: Renovation status and exhibit placement vary over time; verify the specific date.

entries.name: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
entries.era: Opened 1964; museum on the National Mall
entries.geometry: Large modernist museum with broad public entrances and multi-level exhibit circulation
entries.materials: Stone and glass exterior with variable exhibit interiors
capture: Loading and back-of-house zones where publicly documented
entries.cautions: Do not infer restricted back-of-house layouts from public visitor materials.

entries.name: Grand Canyon National Park — South Rim
entries.era: Geological landscape shaped over immense timescales; protected US national park
entries.geometry: Layered canyon topography, cliffs, tributaries, rim overlooks and Colorado River corridor
entries.materials: Sedimentary rock strata, desert soils and variable vegetation
capture: DEM and contour terrain at multiple scales
Rim-to-river elevation differences and geologic stratigraphy
Trail and road access with park restrictions
entries.cautions: The South Rim point is a visitor-area reference, not a single canyon feature; terrain must use elevation data, not photos alone.

entries.name: Lincoln Memorial
entries.geometry: Rectangular Greek Doric temple with broad staircase and central statue chamber
entries.materials: Marble, limestone and granite used in different parts of the monument
capture: Exterior column rhythm and measured elevations
Reflecting Pool alignment and monumental steps
Interior chamber, inscriptions and Lincoln statue scale
Stone jointing, weathering and day/night lighting
entries.cautions: Confirm material placement and precise dimensions with National Park Service or measured drawings.

entries.name: Great Wall of China
entries.era: Fortifications built and rebuilt over many centuries; visible sections often Ming-period
entries.geometry: Long linear fortification adapting to mountain ridges, with watchtowers and stepped battlements
entries.materials: Stone, brick and rammed earth vary by region and period
capture: Choose a specific section before modeling
entries.cautions: Do not represent a single wall section as typical of the entire Great Wall.

entries.name: Petra
entries.era: Nabataean monumental city with later Roman and Byzantine history
entries.geometry: Rock-cut facades, narrow Siq passage, carved tombs and urban archaeological remains
entries.materials: Sandstone cliffs with variable erosion and color
entries.cautions: Petra also belongs to the Ancient Relic Cities layer; use one shared geographic reference.

entries.name: Colosseum
entries.geometry: Elliptical amphitheatre with tiered seating, arcaded exterior and substructure
entries.materials: Travertine, tuff, brick-faced concrete and later repairs
entries.cautions: Distinguish surviving fabric from speculative reconstructions.

entries.name: Chichén Itzá
entries.era: Major Maya center with multiple construction periods
entries.geometry: Ceremonial plazas, stepped pyramids, temples and ballcourts
capture: El Castillo stair and terrace modules
entries.cautions: Avoid conflating distinct construction periods or sacred interpretations.

entries.name: Machu Picchu
entries.era: Fifteenth-century Inca site in the Andes
entries.geometry: Terraced mountain settlement with precise stone masonry and steep topography
entries.cautions: Preserve the mountain setting; do not infer inaccessible interiors.

entries.name: Taj Mahal
entries.geometry: Symmetrical charbagh gardens, marble mausoleum, minarets and flanking structures
entries.materials: White marble, inlaid stone and red sandstone in surrounding structures
entries.cautions: Verify decorative patterns and materials at close range before texture production.

entries.name: Christ the Redeemer
entries.geometry: Art Deco statue on a pedestal overlooking Rio de Janeiro
entries.materials: Reinforced concrete structure clad in soapstone mosaic

research_sources.title: UNESCO — Rio de Janeiro cultural landscape

entries.cautions: Account for changing cloud cover and long-distance visibility.
